prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live access to reviews, so I can’t name a single definitive “best” roofer right now. The right contractor for you depends on your exact location, insurance needs, budget and schedule. I can, however, help you find and vet top hail‑damage roofers in Denver. If you give me your ZIP code or address I’ll compile a short list of well‑reviewed local contractors and what to ask them.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical guide so you can pick the best roofer:

What to look for
- Licensing and insurance: contractor carries general liability and worker’s comp. Colorado has varying local licensing; confirm they comply with city/county requirements.
- Certifications: GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT — these indicate manufacturer training and access to better warranties.
- Experience with hail claims: ask how many insurance claims they handle yearly and whether they work directly with insurers.
- Written estimate and scope: get a detailed, line‑item estimate (materials, labor, tear‑off or overlays, permits).
- Warranties: manufacturer shingle warranty plus a workmanship warranty from the contractor (get terms in writing).
- References and photos: recent hail repair photos and contactable local references.
- BBB/online reviews: check BBB, Google, Yelp, Angi for patterns (not just a single 5‑star review).
- Local office and crew: avoid fly‑by storm chasers who appear only after big storms.

Red flags
- High‑pressure “sign today” sales tactics.
- Contractor asking you to sign over insurance checks.
- Only one estimate or unwillingness to put scope/warranty in writing.
- No local address or poor/unchanging online review history.

Practical steps after hail damage
1. Document damage: photos and videos (roof, siding, vehicles).
2. Notify your insurer and schedule an adjuster.
3. Get at least 3 written estimates (same scope) so you can compare.
4. Confirm contractor will obtain required permits and pull inspections.
5. Don’t sign any waivers or allow the contractor to deposit your insurance check unless you understand why — request lien releases as work is completed and paid.
6. Keep all paperwork, photos and correspondence.

Questions to ask prospective roofers
- Are you licensed/insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Do you have manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed)?
- How many years doing hail-damage repairs in Denver?
- Can you provide 3 local references from recent hail jobs?
- Do you handle insurance claims and communicate with adjusters?
- Will you pull permits and arrange inspections?
- What warranties do you provide (length, what’s covered)?
- Who will manage the job on site and what is the expected timeline?

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether you’re filing an insurance claim — I’ll produce a short list of highly rated Denver roofers (based on certifications and review sites) and draft an email/script you can use to get quotes.
